grh_9e95c9df064d59f6a625.title: Flying Fortress
paragraphs: A Ceiling Unlimited wartime feature devoted to the Flying Fortress. Welles combines the account of an American bomber surviving devastating combat damage with a dramatized tour in which Leonardo da Vinci encounters the modern aircraft and the industrial system behind it. The program explains the plane's engines, armament, factory tooling, production growth, ground crews and flight crew before following a new Fortress eastward toward wartime service. Its central theme is aviation as both technological achievement and a weapon in defense of freedom.
GRH catalogs [[show|the-mercury-theatre-on-the-air|The Mercury Theatre on the Air]]'s "Flying Fortress" for November 9, 1942, as episode 1.
For broader context, GRH's show profile notes: Frozen GRH row is an Orson Welles radio archive container, not a single 1938-1950 series.
GRH classifies the program with genres of drama, format anthology drama, and tone dramatic.
